subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: FINEX latency & throughput requirements
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.in>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.in>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.in>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: throughput & latency summary (FINEX)

Alex - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Goals we heard: steady-state throughput ~120 QPS, peak bursts up to ~600 QPS; average payload ~900 tokens/request; 95th pct latency target around 300ms for non-streaming responses. Streaming required for progressive results on some flows (partial transcript streaming).
- Open questions: percent of requests that must be streaming vs non-streaming, concurrency per client (typical user sessions), and acceptable warmup behavior for peak bursts.

What we’d like from you:
1) Confirm percent of requests that require streaming (ballpark %).
2) Confirm concurrency per user/session (avg and max).
3) Any regulatory or network constraints around sustained connections (for streaming).

Attached: initial sizing workbook and call recording. I’d propose we model two configs: a dedicated pool for peak handling + autoscale for sustained bursts, and a managed shared pool with reserved concurrency for predictable latency.

Next step: I’d like to run a quick tokens/sec/QPS calc and send a recommendation by tomorrow. Would a 30-min follow-up on Tue work to review the sizing and cost tradeoffs?

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: finex_throughput_calc.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
Attachment: call_recording_20270418.mp3 (audio stub)

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.in>
Cc: Procurement <procure@finex.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: throughput & latency summary (FINEX)

Rafael - great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:

- Streaming: roughly 30% of requests need streaming (real-time progress updates for our UI). The other 70% can be non-streaming.
- Concurrency: per human agent session we see ~2 concurrent requests on average; during high load automated jobs we’ve hit up to ~1,200 concurrent connections (these are shorter, smaller prompts).
- Tokens: 900 tokens avg for user-facing requests; automated jobs average 250 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 300ms is our target for user-facing non-streaming responses; streaming latency should start delivering first chunk within 150ms.
- Peak profile: daily peaks last ~10-20 minutes and coincide with end-of-day batch runs that can spike QPS by 4-5x.

We’d like sizing options that prioritize meeting the 95th pct target consistently (even during peaks) and an option that prioritizes lower cost with slightly relaxed SLOs.

Also, yes please include model variant recommendations (FP16 vs 4-bit quantized) and any CPU vs GPU tradeoffs for batching.

Alex
Head of Platform
FinEx

---
Note: please route procurement questions to procure@finex.com for the official SOW/PO path.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.in>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.in>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.in>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: throughput & latency summary (FINEX)

Alex - appreciate the details. I ran an initial tokens/sec and QPS calc (attached) and sketched two recommended configs:

Option A (Performance-first):
- Dedicated GPU pool (8 x A100-equivalent slots), pre-warmed, continuous batching tuned for 900-token avg payloads.
- Target concurrent requests handled: 1,200 sustained with headroom for 4-5x short bursts via reserved burst capacity.
- Expected tokens/sec capacity: ~1,080,000 tokens/sec (approx) across the pool -> ~120 QPS @ 900 tokens, headroom for peaks.
- P95 latency estimate (non-streaming): ~180-260ms depending on model variant and quantization.

Option B (Cost-first):
- Mixed shared pool with quantized model variants (4-bit) and aggressive batching, plus a small dedicated reserve for low-latency paths.
- Expected P95: ~300-450ms under peak; lower cost but higher latency tail risk.

Streaming notes:
- For 30% streaming traffic we recommend a separate streaming-optimized node group that keeps persistent connections and routes streaming requests there to avoid head-of-line blocking in batchers.

Questions to finalize sizing:
- Confirm % of total token volume that comes from automated jobs vs user-facing (affects batch mix).
- Confirm acceptable warmup time for scaling to peak (can Redwood pre-warm if you can share expected spike windows?).

I’d also recommend a canary rollout with an automated fallback to a quantized-compatible variant in case of regressed latency/cost. I’ve attached the calc workbook (finex_throughput_calc.xlsx) and our short sizing notes.

Can we schedule a 30-min call Tue 4/20 10:00am PT to walk through the numbers and procurement steps? I’ll bring our solutions engineer to cover streaming implementation details.

Thanks,
Rafael
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.in>

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call: throughput & latency summary (FINEX)

Looping in a quick internal summary and ask - posting here so the whole thread has context for Alex as well.

- Recommended default: go with Option A for initial rollout to guarantee SLOs; present Option B as a cost-optimization path after 30 days of telemetry.
- Canary plan: 5% traffic canary to the new model variant for first 48 hours, automated rollback if P95 > 350ms or error rate increases >0.5%.
- Streaming: create separate routing policy for streaming requests (30% of traffic). Use persistent connections with per-connection concurrency limits.
- Procurement: Rafael, please include an estimated monthly committed spend for Option A and the MSRP for burst capacity. Procurement will need a draft SOW + DocuSign link.

I'll join Tue's call if possible.

Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
